# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-ref-intents

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

`coop --git` (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote) with the frozen reference settings (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, `medium` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, `-c 4` concurrency) on the 10-pair `core` subset (spanning Python, Go, Rust, and TypeScript), adding `message_intents: true` and `intent_presubmit_check: true` (`configs/variants/message_intents_medium.yaml`). Compares directly against the [`coop --git` `core` reference baseline](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-ref/summary.md) (5/10).

## Observations

- **5/10 (50%) passed (5/10 clean-merge passes, 0 merge conflicts, 0 step-limit cutoffs, 0 agent errors)** at `$18.51` (`64` min, `9` retries), matching the [`coop --git` `core` reference baseline](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-ref/summary.md) (`5/10 = 50%`) with **10/10 identical pair outcomes** (`0` wins, `0` losses).
- **12.7% fewer total messages (25.0% lower median messages per pair), 35.7% fewer compactions, 14.4% lower cost, and 41.8% faster wall time than `core-ref`**: explicit intent tags (`Proposal`, `Request`, `Response`, `ACK`, `FYI`) reduced total messages sent from `307` (median `32`/pair) to `268` (median `24`/pair), compactions from `28` to `18`, run cost from `$21.62` to `$18.51`, and wall time from `110` min to `64` min across the same 10 pairs.
